introduction: The Constitution is divided into Parts, which contain specific Articles. Parts I to IVA (Articles 1 to 51A) form the absolute core of the Indian Constitution, establishing the nation's territory, citizenship rules, fundamental rights of the people, the state's duties, and the citizens' duties.

core_concepts.title: Part I: Union and its Territory (Art 1-4)
core_concepts.description: Article 1: Describes India, that is Bharat, as a 'Union of States'. It establishes the name and type of polity.

core_concepts.title: Part II: Citizenship (Art 5-11)
core_concepts.description: Deals with citizenship at the time of the commencement of the Constitution. Article 11 gives Parliament the ultimate power to make laws regarding citizenship.

core_concepts.title: Part III: Fundamental Rights (Art 12-35)
core_concepts.description: The most frequently asked articles. Art 14: Equality before the law. Art 17: Abolition of Untouchability. Art 21: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty. Art 32: Right to Constitutional Remedies (the power to issue Writs).

core_concepts.title: Part IV: Directive Principles of State Policy (Art 36-51)
core_concepts.description: Guidelines for the government. Art 40: Organization of Village Panchayats. Art 44: Uniform Civil Code (UCC) for the citizens. Art 51: Promotion of international peace and security.

core_concepts.title: Part IVA: Fundamental Duties (Art 51A)
core_concepts.description: Added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Article 51A lists the 11 fundamental duties of every citizen of India.

important_entities.name: Article 32
important_entities.key_fact: Heart and Soul of the Constitution
important_entities.significance: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the heart and soul of the Constitution because it allows citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court if their rights are violated.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Remember the stark difference: Articles in Part III (Fundamental Rights) are enforceable by courts. Articles in Part IV (DPSP) and Part IVA (Fundamental Duties) are NOT enforceable by courts.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: U = Union (Part I), C = Citizenship (Part II), F = Fundamental Rights (Part III), D = Directive Principles (Part IV), F = Fundamental Duties (Part IVA).

exam_strategy_tips: Articles 14, 17, 21, 32, 40, and 51A are the absolute 'must-know' articles. Memorize them first.
A frequent MCQ asks which Article deals with the Abolition of Untouchability. The answer is always Article 17.
